cards.text: The next day, Jesus and the disciples with Him come down from the mountain. A large crowd meets Him at the bottom. It's like coming back from one day off to 300 emails, except these emails have FEET.
Suddenly a man in the crowd cries out. He begs Jesus to look at his son, his only child.

cards.question: What's wrong with the man's only son?

answers.text: A fever will not leave him
He has been blind from birth

cards.text: The father lays it all out. The spirit makes the boy scream, throws him into convulsions until he foams at the mouth, keeps mauling him, and rarely leaves him.

cards.question: Before Jesus came down the mountain, the father begged Jesus' ___ to drive the spirit out.

cards.text: And they were unable. Jesus replies, “O unbelieving and perverse generation!”

cards.question: Jesus asks, “How long must I remain with you and put up with you?” Then what does He tell the father?

answers.text: Go home and he will be well
Wait for Me in the town

cards.text: Even while the boy is on his way over, the demon slams him to the ground in a convulsion. Friend, that spirit is NOT going quietly.

cards.question: The demon slams the boy to the ground while he's still on his way to Jesus. What does Jesus do?

answers.text: Rebukes the spirit and heals the boy
Tells His disciples to try again
Sends the boy to see the priest

cards.question: Once the boy is healed, Jesus gives him back to his father.

cards.text: Everyone is astonished at the greatness of God. And while they're all marveling, Jesus tells His disciples, “Let these words sink into your ears: The Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men.”

cards.question: The disciples understand right away what Jesus means about the Son of Man being delivered into the hands of men.

cards.text: It's veiled from them so they can't comprehend it, and they're afraid to ask Him about it. You know that meeting where the boss says something heavy, everybody nods real slow, and NOBODY raises a hand?

cards.question: Then an argument starts among the disciples. What's it about?

answers.text: Which of them would be the greatest
Which of them should carry the money
Which town they should go to next

cards.text: But Jesus knows the thoughts of their hearts. He doesn't say a word yet. He just has someone come stand beside Him.

cards.question: While the disciples argue about who's the greatest, who does Jesus have stand beside Him?
Jesus says whoever welcomes this little child in His name is welcoming ___.

cards.text: And Jesus keeps going: whoever welcomes Him welcomes the One who sent Him. Then He speaks right to that argument.

cards.question: Jesus tells the arguing disciples that whoever is the least among them is the greatest.

cards.text: Then John speaks up. “Master,” he says, and he tells Jesus about a man they saw doing something in His name.

cards.question: John tells Jesus they saw a man doing something in Jesus' name. What was the man doing?
The disciples tried to stop the man driving out demons in Jesus' name. Why, according to John?

answers.text: He was not traveling with them
He was one of the Pharisees

cards.question: “Do not stop him,” Jesus replies. His reason: whoever is not ___ you is for you.

findings.problem: The passage starts mid-thought with 'The next day, when they came down from the mountain,' but the opening card never says what happened on the mountain or who went up with Jesus. The baker isn't told why they're coming down.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: This story card is 3 sentences: 'But Jesus knows the thoughts of their hearts. He doesn't say a word yet. He just has someone come stand beside Him.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: John shows up for the first time in this passage, but the card doesn't say who he is (for example, John, one of the twelve disciples).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card is a flat retelling with no Papa Dorin voice. A desperate father begging for his only child is a moment that could carry warmth or a reaction from Papa Dorin.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card is a stripped-down list of symptoms with no Papa Dorin voice or reaction.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: 'And they were unable.' followed by the quote reads as bare text with no Papa Dorin voice. The disciples' failure is a moment that could carry a reaction.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Only three story cards across both stops have any humor (Stop 1 card 1, Stop 1 card 8 and Stop 2 card 3). The rest read as neutral narration. Moments like the disciples arguing about who's greatest right after Jesus' announcement (Stop 2, around cards 4-5), or John reporting that they stopped someone (Stop 2 card 10), could hold a real laugh about the disciples' human situation without muddying a fact.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
